name: Le Travenues Technology Ltd
title: Le Travenues Technology Ltd - 544192 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Core GTV grew 22% to INR5,304 crore but flights take rate fell 9.4% to 7% on discounts, hotels still loss-making (contribution -15% of revenue), and PAT was flattered by a Freshbus stake-sale gain.

triggers.label: Flight take rate 9.4% → 7%
triggers.quote: Gross take rate fell from 9.4% to 7% as the base payer and the international mix increased.

triggers.label: Hotel GTV 2.6x, take rate above 12%
triggers.quote: hotel GTV grew 2.6x to INR 111.34 crores, with approximately 4.7 lakh room nights and a gross take rate of over 12%

triggers.label: Hotel investment ~INR10-12 crore/quarter
triggers.quote: Think of a similar range as this quarter, which is between INR 10 crores and INR 12 crores.

guidance.quote: Think of a similar range as this quarter, which is between INR 10 crores and INR 12 crores.
even in the next 4 quarters, our target will be to continue growing in triple digits if we can
Over the next 3 to 4 quarters, you will see them edge up for sure.

red_flags.label: Adj. EBITDA down 17% YoY
red_flags.quote: Adjusted EBITDA was INR23.58 crores against INR28.48 crores a year ago, down 17%.

red_flags.label: PAT inflated by one-off Freshbus gain
red_flags.quote: Reported PAT was INR63.42 crores, but this includes an exceptional gain

red_flags.label: Flight discounts raised to hold share
red_flags.quote: there's a significant portion of our NBU users who make flight bookings, for whom we need to make it more affordable.

summary.headline: ixigo Q2 FY27 GTV rose 22% to INR 5,304 crore and PAT hit a record, but adjusted EBITDA fell 17% to INR 23.6 crore on a stepped-up hotel investment.
summary.overview: Consolidated GTV grew 22% YoY to INR 5,304.47 crore and revenue from operations rose 13% to INR 320.96 crore, with contribution margin up 14% to INR 124.86 crore. Adjusted EBITDA fell 17% to INR 23.58 crore from INR 28.48 crore as management deliberately funded hotel people and technology spend. Reported PAT was an all-time high of INR 63.42 crore, aided by a INR 40.66 crore exceptional gain on the partial sale of Freshbus. Flights were weak: GTV grew 37% on higher fares, but revenue fell 8% as take rate compressed from 9.4% to 7%. Hotels were disclosed as a separate segment for the first time.

financial_highlights.change: All-time high; includes Freshbus exceptional gain of INR 40.66 crore
vs INR 5.17 crore a year ago; treasury income, excluded from adjusted EBITDA

financial_highlights.metric: Net cash incl. FDs and MFs, net of borrowings

segments.name: Trains
segments.commentary: Passenger segments up about 7% to 2.9 crore; revenue up 16% to INR 149.14 crore; CM up 29% to INR 47.23 crore (32% of revenue). OTA rail market share close to 64%. Food on trains moved into trains segment.

segments.name: Buses
segments.commentary: GTV up 32% to INR 752.65 crore; revenue up 24% to INR 81.04 crore; CM up 27% to INR 43.14 crore (53% of revenue).

segments.name: Flights
segments.commentary: GTV up 37% on higher fares, but revenue down 8% to INR 82.66 crore; CM down 10% to INR 35.68 crore, held at 43% of revenue. Take rate fell from 9.4% to 7%. International flight GTV up 59%.

segments.name: Hotels (new disclosure)
segments.commentary: GTV up 2.6x YoY to INR 111.34 crore (up 39% QoQ), about 4.7 lakh room nights, take rate above 12%, revenue INR 8.1 crore. Contribution loss INR 1.21 crore vs INR 0.71 crore a year ago; CM -15% of revenue vs -55% a year ago. Brevistay consolidated from this quarter, so part of growth is inorganic.

guidance_outlook: Hotel investment (above and below CM) was about INR 11 crore this quarter; management expects a similar range of INR 10-12 crore per quarter over the next couple of quarters, not a firm guidance.
Hotel take rate expected to edge up over the next 3-4 quarters; no guidance given on the level for next year.
Hotel room night ambition to keep growing at triple digits over the next four quarters; aim to be largest budget-to-mid-market hotel OTA by room nights in 4-5 years.
Flights: management is not guiding to aggressive growth; October started softer than expected with capacity not yet back, and festive demand is a shade below expectations.
Management says it will not step up flight discounts beyond current fare levels.
Profitability for hotels not targeted near term; investment expected for 2-3 years, with company-level EBITDA kept around mid-single-digit levels.
capex_capacity: Hotel direct supply: over 12,000 directly contracted hotels across about 1,100 towns, up from 10,000 last quarter, out of about 70,000 hotels sold.
Management says it is not in a rush to grow the directly contracted base faster than its own growth.
Hotel share of GTV is about 2.1%; management targets hotels as one of the top two GTV contributors in 4-5 years.
Freshbus stake partly sold on August 13, resulting in a INR 40.66 crore gain; company describes itself as asset-light.
Acquisitions: selective, only where there is strategic fit, team, technology or distribution synergy, and reasonable pricing; will disclose when they crystallise.
demand_pricing: Overall flight market volume down nearly 6% in the quarter; ixigo flight segment grew 7%.
Flight fares up about 30% YoY on several routes due to oil prices; capacity slow to return; load factors edging down.
Flight take rate compression attributed to higher discounts for NBU users, growing international mix and convenience fees forming a larger share of income.
Hotel take rate above 12% blended, versus the 16-17% level seen at other OTAs; higher take rates in mid-tier and independent hotels are the structural argument.
About 86% of hotel bookings came from existing platform users; 94% of transactions involve Tier 2 and 3 cities.
Hotel ATV around INR 2,200 per room night; management does not guide to a specific ATV level.
Trains: festive advance bookings helped; management wants to see momentum persist beyond the festive season before calling the recovery sustained.
Bus growth described as ahead of the overall OTA bus market for close to three years.
AI platform traffic is a low single-digit percentage of traffic for the category; agentic booking flow demoed at GFS, launch awaiting regulatory clarity.

qa_highlights.question: Why did flight revenue per ticket fall 13-14% against the recent average; is this a permanent share-gain strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said higher discounts were needed to keep NBU flight users affordable given the 30% fare rise, and international mix and convenience fees also compressed take rate. It said it would not step up discounts further at current fares.

qa_highlights.question: Is there early visibility on Q3 flight trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Festive demand is a shade lower than expected; management is cautious on flights and not guiding to aggressive growth, but says it will keep growing.

qa_highlights.question: When will hotel take rate reach 16-17% and when will the segment be profitable?
qa_highlights.answer: Take rate will edge up over the next 3-4 quarters as direct supply grows, with no next-year guidance. Profitability is not targeted near term; investment is expected for 2-3 years, with spending tied to observed returns and payback periods.

qa_highlights.question: How should investors frame hotel investment within guardrails?
qa_highlights.answer: Investment was INR 1 crore-plus above CM and about INR 10 crore below CM this quarter. Guardrails are customer payback periods and keeping company-level EBITDA in the mid-single-digit range, with a near-term range of INR 10-12 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What GTV mix can be expected over 3-4 years, and will rail share gains continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Hotels could be the second-largest GTV contributor in 4-5 years. Management expects rail GTV share to decline from the early 40s given 4-5% annual capacity growth; buses to be the second-fastest growing line after hotels.

qa_highlights.question: How much of a threat do consumer AI agents pose, and which segments are most exposed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AI-platform traffic is still a low single-digit share and sees specialist vertical agents, and ixigo's proprietary data and peace-of-mind products as differentiators. Building products is easy; trust and distribution are the hard parts.

qa_highlights.question: Is the bus growth of about 28% too slow given supply and rail constraints?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is comfortable with the current pace, trading growth for margin and a sustainable business, and noted bus CM is about 53% of revenue.

risks_watch: Flight recovery: capacity has not returned, fares are up about 30%, and October started softer than expected.
Hotel economics: blended take rate of 12% is well below the 16-17% at peers; contribution loss is widening in absolute terms and profitability is 2-3 years away.
Adjusted EBITDA down 17%; the reported PAT includes a one-time Freshbus gain, so underlying earnings are weaker than headline.
Rail: management says recovery is not yet proven beyond the festive season; rail GTV share may decline.
AI agents: consumer AI platforms could disintermediate bookings; the agentic booking flow awaits regulatory clarity before launch.
Inorganic: Brevistay consolidation adds to hotel growth; future acquisitions are unspecified.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the core business, buses and the hotel opportunity, but cautious on flights and near-term festive demand. Management was direct about the deliberate step-up in hotel investment, yet gave no firm profitability timeline and deflected several questions on hotel take rate and ATV.
key_quotes: Flights faced a tougher external environment with high fares and limited capacity affecting bookings growth, and the overall market was down nearly 6% in volume terms in the quarter.
But right now, what I'll say is our investment will go hand-in-hand with our growth.
Repeatability comes from what problem you are solving.

growth.why: Management guides hotel room-night growth to stay in triple digits for the next four quarters and hotel take rate to edge up over 3-4 quarters, backed by 12,000+ directly contracted hotels, but gives no firm hotel revenue target; flights are explicitly not guided to aggressive growth and company-level EBITDA is kept around mid-single-digit margins.
